name: Windows utilities · System tray tools
description: System tray utilities for long-lived Windows background tasks: least privilege, signing, and graceful degradation when session state changes.
longDescription: Lightweight utilities for background tasks reachable from the Windows system tray without a full application window. Tray-resident code is treated as high visibility on the endpoint: failures should be quiet but observable, and privileges should stay minimal unless a feature explicitly requires elevation.
features: System tray interaction patterns without unnecessary foreground windows
Defensive handling when tray APIs or session state are unavailable
Scoped utilities within a shared automation monorepo
highlights: Always-available helpers from the system tray
challenges: Tray apps must fail gracefully when permissions or session state changes.
solutions: Document startup requirements and handle missing tray APIs defensively.
security: Sign binaries and minimise privileges for tray-resident code
Avoid storing secrets in tray-accessible configuration
